analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. changelog.d/qwen-gdn-prompt-kernel.md (head 1-4) is a new changelog entry. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md changes the date (line 3) and adds the 'GDN prompt kernels by GPU' section (head 527-555).

The text describes a new Gated DeltaNet four-row prefill kernel for Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 and Bonsai 2 prompt chunks of 16 or more tokens. A runtime GPU probe (GatedDeltaPrefill.probe in libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/GatedDelta.swift) is said to select the candidate only when its output is bit-exact with stock gated_delta_step. Otherwise the stock kernel is kept. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED=0 is the rollback, forwarded by darkbloom start to launchd providers. The probe's transient allocation is stated as at most about 16 MiB once per instantiation. No capacity, KV grant or admission fields are said to change.

Threat relevance:
- T-007/T-027 (output integrity): the bit-exactness claim means outputs should be unchanged; this is not a security control.
- T-041 (prefix cache): the recurrent-checkpoint compatibility claim matters because checkpoints are stored in SSD prefix-cache entries. A kernel that is not bit-exact could cause cross-kernel checkpoint incompatibility, a correctness/availability issue rather than disclosure.
- Memory/DoS (T-016/T-029 class): the roughly 16 MiB transient appears to be outside ledger accounting. It is small, so no finding.

No security regression is visible in the docs. Kernel implementation source is not supplied, which is a coverage limit. Integration should verify:
- the probe is genuinely bit-exact and covers all eligible dtypes and geometries, not just one 32-position window;
- probe allocation goes through, or is bounded relative to, ProcessMemoryLedger;
- probe failure or race falls back to the stock kernel;
- the environment-variable parsing defaults safely and its forwarding by darkbloom start adds no injection surface.
